title: Prove |F_w| is homeomorphic to S^2 (not merely chi = 2)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap D.** From the cell structure (5 vertices, 6 edges, 3 squares; $\chi=5-6+3=2$) prove $|F_w|\cong S^2$. **Euler characteristic alone is insufficient** (it cannot by itself exclude non-manifold pinch points, wedges, or non-orientable possibilities with the same $\chi$).

Provide one of:
(i) Show $F_w$ is a closed surface: every 1-cell lies on exactly two 2-cells (no boundary), and the link of every 0-cell is a single circle (manifold point); then show it is connected and orientable, and conclude $S^2$ by the classification of compact surfaces.
(ii) Construct an explicit cellular homeomorphism to a standard CW structure on $S^2$ (e.g. boundary of a triangular bipyramid).
(iii) Compute $H_*(F_w)$ and $\pi_1$: show $\pi_1=1$ (van Kampen) and $H_2=\mathbb{Z}$, so $F_w$ is a simply connected closed surface with $H_2=\mathbb{Z}$, hence $\simeq S^2$.

The genuine content is ruling out non-manifold/wedge points via the link conditions.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolved (Gap D / option (i)).** The closed-surface argument in Proposition \ref{prop:s2} now rigorously rules out non-manifold pinch points, wedges, and non-orientable possibilities; it does *not* rely on $\chi=2$ alone.

What is established (all checked numerically over the 15 pairings of $P$):

1. **No boundary:** every $1$-cell $E_k$ is a face of *exactly two* $2$-cells (incidence table \eqref{eq:faces}; a script confirms `edge -> squares` is 2-valued for all six edges).

2. **Manifold at edge-interiors:** since $F_w$ is a *regular* CW complex (Prop. \ref{prop:W3}), each edge is glued into each incident square as a single facet, so the two incident squares contribute two half-disks glued along the edge = an open disk. Free edges (1 square) and book-with-$\ge3$-pages (3+ squares) are explicitly excluded.

3. **Manifold at vertices (the genuine content):** the link graph $\Lambda(Q)$ is shown to be connected and 2-regular, i.e. a single cycle, for every vertex. Verified: $\Lambda(Q_1),\Lambda(Q_4)$ are 3-cycles; $\Lambda(Q_2),\Lambda(Q_3),\Lambda(Q_5)$ are bigons (two nodes joined by two arcs — still a circle). All node-degrees are exactly 2. This is precisely what rules out pinch/wedge points (which would give a disconnected link or a node of degree != 2).

4. **Connected** (spanning tree $E_3,E_2,E_1,E_4$ on the 5 vertices).

5. **Classification:** $|F_w|$ is therefore a compact, connected, boundaryless topological $2$-manifold. By the classification of compact surfaces and $\chi=2$, it is $S^2$. I made explicit that orientability need not be checked separately: no non-orientable closed surface has $\chi=2$ ($\chi(N_k)=2-k\le1$), so $\chi=2$ already forces $S^2$.

6. **Homological confirmation:** independent $\mathbb{Z}/2$-homology gives Betti numbers $(1,0,1)$, matching $S^2$; in particular $H_2\ne0$ so $F_w$ is not contractible.

Edits: the "$F_w$ is a closed surface" and "Identification" paragraphs of Prop. \ref{prop:s2} were rewritten to make the manifold-point reasoning explicit (cone-on-link criterion; single-facet gluing from regularity). All link/incidence/attaching data re-verified by exhaustive script. Gap closed.
